mood.summary: Fear is still running high. On Nov 5 the S&P 500 fell 4.4% and the Nasdaq slid into a correction, the worst day since April 2025, on worries that election results will slow AI and data-centre spending. The Fear & Greed index sits in Extreme Fear at 20, and bearish individual investors outnumber bulls by about 14 points. Stocks are bouncing on Nov 6 after a strong jobs report (165,000 jobs vs about 60,000 expected), but that also firmed bets on a December Fed rate hike.

trending.note: Board as of Wednesday 4:05 PM ET; prices are the 2026-11-18 close. Why-it's-trending notes summarize the Stocktwits stream and the news it links to.

items.name: UnitedHealth Group
items.about: Largest US health insurer, also running the Optum health-services and pharmacy-benefits businesses.
items.why: Shares fell about 10% for a second straight drop after CMS proposed a rule (posted Nov 16) that would reopen Medicare Advantage payment audits back to 2018, which CMS estimates would recover about $9B a year across the industry. Coverage also cited renewed calls in Congress to break up vertically integrated insurers; UnitedHealth has not quantified its exposure.

items.name: Alibaba Group
items.about: Chinese e-commerce and cloud-computing group behind Taobao, Tmall and Alibaba Cloud.
items.why: Alibaba reports its September-quarter results on Thursday Nov 19 before the US open, and the stock slid about 2.7% into the print after falling nearly 40% this year on AI spending and e-commerce margin worries. Posts also point to a Trump meeting on China later in the week as a possible swing factor.

items.name: SPDR Gold Shares
items.about: Exchange-traded fund that holds physical gold bullion.
items.why: GLD dropped about 3.2% as spot gold fell to its lowest level in more than a year. Hawkish comments from Fed officials raised odds of a December rate hike and lifted the US dollar to a 19-month high, which weighs on dollar-priced metals.

items.name: SELLAS Life Sciences
items.about: Clinical-stage biotech developing cancer immunotherapies, led by galinpepimut-S for leukemia.
items.why: On Nov 17 Sellas said its Phase 3 REGAL trial of galinpepimut-S in AML met its overall-survival goal (median 24.0 vs 14.7 months, about 41% lower risk of death), and the stock roughly tripled. It gave back about 6% on Wednesday; the company plans a BLA filing in the first half of 2027, and posts say traders fear a stock offering.

items.name: Palo Alto Networks
items.about: Cybersecurity company selling firewalls and cloud and AI security platforms.
items.why: Shares jumped about 10.5% into fiscal Q1 results due after Wednesday's close, as cybersecurity stocks rallied; analysts expected about $3.31B in revenue and $0.97 adjusted EPS. The stock had fallen after its last four reports, and posts after the bell say it gave back part of the gain and announced another acquisition, which was not yet confirmed at this update.

items.name: NVIDIA
items.about: Largest maker of AI accelerator chips and data-center computing systems.
items.why: Nvidia's Q3 revenue rose 103% to about $115.8B, ahead of the roughly $109B consensus, and it guided to about $130B next quarter; this was its first report since Jensen Huang stepped down. The stock opened higher but closed about 3% lower near $151, with gross margin guided down to 71–72% and no China data-center sales assumed.

items.name: Take-Two Interactive
items.about: Video-game publisher behind Grand Theft Auto, Red Dead Redemption and NBA 2K.
items.why: Grand Theft Auto VI reviews landed at 99 on Metacritic, tied for the highest score ever, a day before Thursday's launch, and the stock rebounded about 6% after two losing sessions. Wells Fargo raised its net-bookings forecast by 19%, and posts cite pre-order estimates of about $1.5B.

items.name: Skydance Corp. (Paramount Skydance)
items.about: Media company formed from Paramount, Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery, owning CBS, studios and streaming services.
items.why: Shares slid about 4% to an all-time low near $6.63, extending a drop that began after its first combined quarterly report on Nov 9, when it warned that weak Warner Bros. and Paramount film results would offset streaming growth. The stock is down about 40% this year, and posts focus on its heavy debt load.

items.name: Capricor Therapeutics
items.about: Biotech developing deramiocel, a cell therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
items.why: The FDA's decision on deramiocel is due by Nov 22 after the deadline was pushed back three months for a revised filing focused on upper-limb function. Shares swung between about $8 and $9.48 and closed about 4.5% lower; an FDA advisory panel earlier voted mostly against approval for DMD cardiomyopathy, and posts say a trading halt may precede news.

items.name: Riot Platforms
items.about: Bitcoin miner converting part of its power capacity into data centers for AI and high-performance computing.
items.why: Riot rose about 7% after activist investor Starboard Value pitched the stock at the C4K Investors Conference, per Seeking Alpha. The bull case centers on repurposing its Texas power sites for AI data centers, while posts also note miners have been selling bitcoin to fund that shift.

items.name: AST SpaceMobile
items.about: Building a satellite network designed to connect directly to ordinary mobile phones.
items.why: Shares fell about 7.6% after Jim Cramer called it a very hard stock to own, extending a slide that has the stock down about 60% this year. Competition from Amazon's approved Globalstar deal and steady share issuance remain the main bear points in posts.

items.name: IREN Limited
items.about: Data-center operator that has shifted from bitcoin mining to renting GPUs for AI cloud computing.
items.why: IREN fell about 3.7% on unusually heavy volume of about 81M shares as AI-infrastructure stocks stayed under pressure, and the stock is down sharply from about $21.64 after its Nov 6 earnings jump. Posts say the company may be selling shares through its at-the-market program, which was not confirmed.

items.name: Green Thumb Industries
items.about: US cannabis company running Rise dispensaries and consumer brands such as Rythm and Dogwalkers.
items.why: The stock was flat near $5.96 but chatter rose as posts tied Hakeem Jeffries' expected role as House Speaker to hopes for federal cannabis reform. Posts also point to its roughly $316M cash balance and a return to same-store sales growth; these are crowd claims, not company news.

items.name: Fundrise Innovation Fund
items.about: Closed-end venture fund holding late-stage private tech companies, with Anthropic its largest position.
items.why: VCX fell about 3.8% the day before Anthropic's IPO, which was expected to price Wednesday evening and trade on Nasdaq Thursday. Anthropic was more than 20% of the fund's assets as of July, and posts argue that direct shares will reduce the need for proxy vehicles like VCX.

items.name: GEO Group
items.about: Operates private prisons and immigration detention centers, largely under US government contracts.
items.why: GEO hit a 52-week high early after a research note highlighted its sale of a 1,635-bed ICE processing center to the Department of Homeland Security for $453M, then closed about 2.9% lower. Posts point to political risk from incoming House leadership as the reason for the reversal.

items.name: ZIM Integrated Shipping
items.about: Israeli container-shipping company that agreed in February to be acquired by Hapag-Lloyd for $35 a share.
items.why: ZIM reported Q3 EPS of about $6.88 and posts say it raised its 2026 adjusted EBITDA outlook to $3.3–3.5B, but the stock rose only about 0.7% because it trades mostly on the pending $35-a-share Hapag-Lloyd takeover. Posts debate whether Israeli government approval of the deal will come through.

items.name: Lowe's
items.about: Home-improvement retailer serving do-it-yourself customers and contractors.
items.why: Lowe's reported Q3 adjusted EPS of $3.10, above estimates, though about $0.34 came from tariff refunds; comparable sales rose 1.8% and it nudged up full-year sales guidance. The stock dipped as low as about $211 early, then finished about 1% higher.

items.name: Walt Disney
items.about: Entertainment company spanning theme parks, film studios, ESPN and the Disney+ streaming service.
items.why: Disney's fiscal Q4 adjusted EPS of $1.77 and 16% revenue growth to about $25.9B beat forecasts, and it raised its dividend 33% to $2 a share alongside a $3B cost-cut target. At least seven analysts lifted price targets, and the stock closed about 4.6% higher.

items.name: Eaton
items.about: Power-management company making electrical equipment such as switchgear for data centers, utilities and industry.
items.why: Eaton ended up about 0.4% after trading between about $332 and $342, as investors weighed AI data-center power demand against signs of slower AI spending. Posts cite a fund-manager survey in which many expect capital spending cuts, while its last quarter showed sales up 28%.

items.name: Freeport-McMoRan
items.about: One of the world's largest copper miners, with major operations in Indonesia and the Americas.
items.why: Freeport fell about 7% after Erste Group cut it to Hold, citing Grasberg production issues, while copper dropped to its lowest since April. Mining coverage tied the copper slide to an unwind of AI and tariff trades and a stronger dollar.
